docs.title: OVI-CODE
docs.text:
A fast, keyboard-driven coding agent for your terminal.

OVI-CODE is a C++20 terminal application that connects to OpenRouter, OpenAI, Anthropic, or xAI/Grok. It can inspect a workspace, read and edit files, and show every model response, tool call, result, and diff in a full-screen interface.

  • Work in the terminal

    Use a Vim-style multiline editor and keep the conversation, tool activity, and file changes visible in one screen.

  • Choose the right model

    Select a provider account and curated model, enter any custom model ID, and use only the reasoning-effort levels supported by that model.

  • Control the workflow

    Switch between Standard ReAct, Chain of Thought, Ralph Loop, RAG, and runtime-loaded technique plugins.

  • Keep tools in the workspace

    File tools resolve paths inside the selected workspace and reject path traversal outside it.

docs.title: Quick start
docs.text:
brew install --cask Ovicorps/ovi-code/ovi-code
cd /path/to/project
ovi-code

The first launch asks for a provider account, API key, model, reasoning effort, and default technique. Type a request in Insert mode, press Esc to enter Normal mode, then press Enter to send it.

Get started Learn the TUI

docs.title: Core capabilities
docs.text:
• Full-screen TUI built with FTXUI.
  • Vim-style prompt and instruction-file editors.
  • OpenRouter, OpenAI, Anthropic, and xAI/Grok API clients with capability-aware reasoning effort.
  • Workspace-scoped read_file, list_files, and edit_file tools.
  • Project instructions from agent.md, tools.md, and skills.md.
  • Dark, light, system, and high-contrast plain themes.
  • Native C++ technique plugins through a versioned C ABI.

Review agent changes

OVI-CODE can make broad changes inside the selected workspace. Use version control, review diffs, and avoid opening directories that contain unrelated sensitive files.

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
To run OVI-CODE you need an API key and sufficient credits for OpenRouter, OpenAI, Anthropic, or xAI/Grok.

Building from source additionally requires:

  • CMake 3.20 or newer
  • A C++20 compiler
  • System libcurl
  • Git and an internet connection during the first CMake configure

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
HomebrewBuild from source 
brew install --cask Ovicorps/ovi-code/ovi-code

git clone https://github.com/Ovicorps/ovi-code.git
cd ovi-code
cmake -S . -B build -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release
cmake --build build -j

The executable is build/ovi-code. Install it to another prefix with:

cmake --install build --prefix ~/.local

docs.title: Configure
docs.text:
Run the application:

ovi-code

The first launch opens a five-step setup wizard:

  1. Choose a provider account.
  2. Enter that provider's API key.
  3. Choose a curated model or enter a custom provider model ID.
  4. Choose a reasoning effort supported by that model.
  5. Choose the default agentic technique.

Configuration is stored at ~/.ovi-code/config.json with permissions set to 0600. To rerun setup later:

ovi-code --setup

You can keep the key out of the configuration file by setting an environment variable for the selected provider:

export OPENROUTER_API_KEY="sk-or-v1-..."
# Or: OPENAI_API_KEY, ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, XAI_API_KEY
ovi-code

docs.title: Open a workspace
docs.text:
Run OVI-CODE from the project directory:

cd ~/Projects/my-project
ovi-code

Or pass the workspace explicitly:

ovi-code --workspace ~/Projects/my-project

The workspace is the security boundary for built-in file tools. Tool paths that resolve outside it are rejected.

docs.title: Send the first request
docs.text:
The prompt starts in Insert mode. Type a request, press Esc to enter Normal mode, and press Enter to send it.

Find the cause of the build failure, fix it, and rebuild the project.

During a turn, the selected model may answer directly or request file tools. Tool activity is shown in the output panel and returned to the model until it answers or reaches the configured iteration limit.

Conversation context stays in memory for the current process. Restart OVI-CODE to begin a new conversation.

docs.title: Next steps
docs.text:
• Learn keyboard navigation and Settings.
  • Compare the built-in agentic techniques.
  • Add project-specific instructions with agent.md, tools.md, and skills.md.

docs.title: Technique plugins
docs.text:
Technique plugins are native C++ dynamic libraries loaded at process startup. They appear in setup, Settings, and the T technique cycle without linking against OVI-CODE internals.

Plugins execute native code

A plugin has the same operating-system permissions as OVI-CODE. It is not sandboxed. Install only plugins whose source and publisher you trust.

docs.title: Discover plugins
docs.text:
The default plugin directory is:

~/.ovi-code/plugins

Override it with a flag or environment variable:

ovi-code --plugin-dir /path/to/plugins
OVI_CODE_PLUGIN_DIR=/path/to/plugins ovi-code

List loaded modules and loader errors without opening the TUI:

ovi-code plugins
ovi-code plugins --plugin-dir ./build/plugins

OVI-CODE loads .dylib and .so files once at startup. Restart after adding or rebuilding a plugin.

docs.title: Build the example
docs.text:
The repository includes plugins/examples/deliberate.cpp, built by default:

cmake -S . -B build
cmake --build build -j
./build/ovi-code plugins --plugin-dir ./build/plugins
./build/ovi-code --plugin-dir ./build/plugins

docs.title: Write a plugin
docs.text:
Plugins include the dependency-free public ABI header:

#include "ovicode/technique_plugin.h"

#include <string>

namespace {

int runTurn(void*, const OviCodeTechniqueHostV1* host,
            const char* user_input) {
    if (!host || !host->run_react || !user_input) return 0;

    std::string system = host->base_system_prompt;
    system += "\n\nCheck assumptions before every tool call.";
    return host->run_react(host->context, system.c_str(), user_input);
}

const OviCodeTechniquePluginV1 plugin{
    OVI_CODE_TECHNIQUE_PLUGIN_API_VERSION,
    "verify-first",
    "Verify First",
    "Checks assumptions before acting",
    nullptr,
    nullptr,
    runTurn,
};

}  // namespace

extern "C" const OviCodeTechniquePluginV1*
ovi_code_get_technique_plugin_v1() {
    return &plugin;
}
macOSLinux 
mkdir -p ~/.ovi-code/plugins
c++ -std=c++20 -dynamiclib -I/path/to/ovi-code/include \
  verify_first.cpp -o ~/.ovi-code/plugins/verify-first.dylib

mkdir -p ~/.ovi-code/plugins
c++ -std=c++20 -shared -fPIC -I/path/to/ovi-code/include \
  verify_first.cpp -o ~/.ovi-code/plugins/verify-first.so

Plugin IDs must start with a lowercase letter or digit and contain only lowercase letters, digits, ., _, or -. They must not duplicate another plugin or built-in technique ID.

docs.title: Runtime interface
docs.text:
Field or callback Purpose id, label, description Metadata shown and persisted by OVI-CODE create / destroy Optional process-lifetime plugin state run_turn Entry point for each user turn host->workspace Absolute active workspace path host->base_system_prompt Standard prompt plus project instructions host->run_react Run one complete model/tool pass host->last_assistant_text Inspect the latest assistant response host->emit Write System or Error transcript entries host->iteration_limit Maximum host-enforced passes for the turn

Pointers supplied by the host are valid only during run_turn; copy data that must be retained. Never allow C++ exceptions to cross the exported C ABI.

See the exact declarations in technique_plugin.h.

docs.title: CLI reference
docs.text: ovi-code [command] [options]

docs.title: Commands
docs.text: Command Description init Run setup, save configuration, and exit plugins List runtime technique plugins and loader errors uninstall Remove the saved configuration and exit

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Option Description --workspace <dir> Workspace root; defaults to the current directory --agent-config-dir <dir> Directory containing agent.md, tools.md, and skills.md --config <file> Custom application configuration path --plugin-dir <dir> Runtime technique plugin directory --setup Run the setup wizard again --init Alias for init --list-plugins Alias for plugins --uninstall Alias for uninstall --no-splash Skip the startup splash -h, --help Print CLI and keyboard help

docs.title: Environment variables
docs.text: Variable Description OPENROUTER_API_KEY Override the API key saved in configuration OPENAI_API_KEY Override the saved OpenAI API key ANTHROPIC_API_KEY Override the saved Anthropic API key XAI_API_KEY Override the saved xAI/Grok API key OVI_CODE_PLUGIN_DIR Override the runtime plugin directory COLORFGBG Help automatic theme detection determine terminal brightness

docs.title: Files and directories
docs.text:
Path Purpose ~/.ovi-code/config.json Saved settings and provider accounts; mode 0600 ~/.ovi-code/plugins/ Default native technique plugin directory <workspace>/agent.md Project persona, conventions, and constraints <workspace>/tools.md Project-specific tool instructions <workspace>/skills.md Reusable project recipes and capabilities

Use --config, --plugin-dir, or --agent-config-dir to override the relevant default path.

docs.title: Built-in tools
docs.text:
Tool Behavior read_file Read a file relative to the workspace list_files Recursively list workspace files while skipping generated and Git directories edit_file Replace one unique occurrence or create a file

All tool paths pass through the workspace path-traversal guard. This protects files outside the workspace, but the agent can still make broad changes inside it.

docs.title: Build commands
docs.text:
cmake -S . -B build -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release
cmake --build build -j
cmake --install build --prefix ~/.local

CMake fetches FTXUI and nlohmann/json during the first configure and links against system libcurl.

docs.title: Agentic techniques
docs.text:
Techniques change the control flow around the selected provider client and workspace tools. Choose one in Settings or press T from chat Normal mode.

Technique Behavior Suggested use Standard ReAct Alternates between model responses and tool calls until the model answers Most coding tasks Chain of Thought Adds a step-by-step reasoning instruction before the ReAct loop Multi-step diagnosis and planning Ralph Loop Reissues the same goal for a configured number of passes and stops early on DONE Iterative refactors and repeated improvement RAG Searches the workspace for query keywords and prepends matching excerpts Large or unfamiliar projects

docs.title: Execution limits
docs.text:
The Agent Settings tab controls safeguards around technique execution:

  • Tool-call limit caps tool iterations in one standard ReAct pass.
  • Ralph passes caps goal repetitions in Ralph Loop.
  • Plugin passes caps host ReAct passes requested by a runtime plugin.
  • Temperature controls sampling when the model supports it. A negative value omits the provider temperature parameter.

docs.title: Models and reasoning effort
docs.text:
The curated model picker records supported reasoning levels for each known model. Settings only shows valid levels for the current selection.

Auto follows model capabilities. If a saved effort is unavailable after a model change, OVI-CODE uses that model's automatic behavior rather than sending an invalid effort.

Unknown custom model IDs expose only Auto because their capabilities are not in the local curated list.

docs.title: Choosing a technique
docs.text:
• Start with Standard ReAct for normal implementation and debugging.
  • Use Chain of Thought when a task benefits from explicit decomposition.
  • Use Ralph Loop when the model should inspect and improve its result over several passes.
  • Use RAG when likely-relevant code needs to be surfaced before the first model response.
  • Use a technique plugin for custom orchestration that must run without changing the OVI-CODE binary.

docs.title: Provider authentication fails
docs.text:
Confirm the Model Settings tab contains the selected provider's key, or set OPENROUTER_API_KEY, OPENAI_API_KEY, ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, or XAI_API_KEY. OpenRouter keys must begin with sk-or-v1-. To rerun setup:

ovi-code --setup

docs.title: The wrong project is open
docs.text:
Quit and restart with an explicit workspace:

ovi-code --workspace /absolute/path/to/project

docs.title: Output does not scroll
docs.text: Press Esc to enter Normal mode, Ctrl+W to focus output, then use J, K, G, or Shift+G.

docs.title: The terminal appears frozen
docs.text: Many terminals reserve Ctrl+S and Ctrl+Q for XON/XOFF flow control. OVI-CODE does not bind those keys, but accidentally pressing Ctrl+S can pause terminal output. Press Ctrl+Q to resume it.

docs.title: Colors have poor contrast
docs.text: Open the Appearance Settings tab and choose Dark, Light, or Plain instead of automatic detection. Plain uses a fixed, high-contrast monochrome palette.

docs.title: Project instructions are ignored
docs.text:
Confirm agent.md, tools.md, and skills.md are in the workspace root, or pass their directory explicitly:

ovi-code --agent-config-dir /path/to/instructions

Changes are loaded at the start of the next turn.

docs.title: A model request fails
docs.text:
Confirm that:

  • The model ID exists for the selected provider.
  • The selected provider account has sufficient credits.
  • The selected provider API is reachable.
  • The selected model supports the requested operation.

Try a curated model from the Model Settings tab to rule out an invalid custom model ID.

docs.title: A plugin does not appear
docs.text:
Run the plugin listing command with the same directory used by the TUI:

ovi-code plugins --plugin-dir /path/to/plugins

Check the reported loader errors, platform extension (.dylib on macOS or .so on Linux), exported symbol, ABI version, and plugin ID. Restart OVI-CODE after rebuilding the module.

docs.title: Reset configuration
docs.text:
Remove the saved configuration and run setup again:

ovi-code uninstall
ovi-code

For a Homebrew installation, remove both the application and saved data with:

brew uninstall --cask --zap ovi-code

docs.title: Using the TUI
docs.text: The chat screen contains an output panel for conversation and tool activity, and an input panel with a multiline Vim-style prompt editor. The highlighted panel title indicates keyboard focus.

docs.title: Insert mode
docs.text: Key Action Characters Insert text Enter Insert a newline Tab Insert four spaces Arrow keys Move the cursor Home / End Move to the start / end of the line Backspace / Del Delete text Esc Enter Normal mode

docs.title: Normal mode
docs.text:
Key Action H / J / K / L Move left / down / up / right W / B Move forward / backward by word 0 / $ Move to the start / end of the line G G / Shift+G Move to the first / last line I / A Insert before / after the cursor Shift+I / Shift+A Insert at the start / end of the line O / Shift+O Open a line below / above X Delete the character under the cursor D D Delete the current line Y Y Copy the current line P / Shift+P Paste after / before the current line Enter Send the prompt Ctrl+W Switch between input and output Z Minimize or restore the input panel S Open Settings T Cycle the selected technique C Clear the visible transcript Q Quit

The internal line clipboard is shared by the prompt, tools.md, and skills.md editors.

docs.title: Output navigation
docs.text:
Press Ctrl+W in Normal mode to focus the output panel.

Key Action J / K Scroll down / up G / Shift+G Jump to the top / bottom Ctrl+W Return to the input panel

The application shortcuts S, T, C, and Q remain available while output is focused.

docs.title: Settings
docs.text:
Press S from Normal mode. Settings are organized into four tabs:

Tab Contents Model Provider account, model, reasoning effort, and provider API key Agent Technique, execution limits, temperature, and instruction editors Appearance System, dark, light, and plain themes Shortcuts Chat and Settings keyboard reference

Use Tab to move between controls (or cycle a focused list) and J / K or arrow keys to change list selections. Press Enter to activate a focused button, or I / A before typing in a text field.

Save changes applies the configuration to the next turn. Cancel, Q, or Esc from Normal mode closes Settings without applying the form.

docs.title: Project instructions
docs.text:
OVI-CODE reads three optional Markdown files from the workspace root:

File Purpose agent.md Project persona, conventions, constraints, and hard rules tools.md Additional guidance for using tools skills.md Reusable recipes and project-specific capabilities

Use another directory when instructions should live outside the workspace:

ovi-code \
  --workspace ~/Projects/my-project \
  --agent-config-dir ~/Projects/my-project/.ovi-code

Instruction files are reloaded at the beginning of every turn. Settings provides built-in editors for tools.md and skills.md; use S to save and Q to cancel from those editors.

docs.title: Privacy and session data
docs.text:
• Provider keys are stored in ~/.ovi-code/config.json unless supplied through OPENROUTER_API_KEY, OPENAI_API_KEY, ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, or XAI_API_KEY.
  • Chat history is not persisted to disk.
  • Clearing the transcript with C does not clear model conversation context.
  • Requests, instructions, and file contents returned by tools are sent to the selected provider. OpenRouter may route them to a separate model provider.
